summary: Forgot Password (in-app code) end-to-end review for Kite Trivia. Extended pytest suite from 16 → 23 tests covering forgot-password (registered/unregistered/rate-cap) and reset-password (happy path / invalid code / single-use / short password). All 23 backend pytest tests PASS. Full frontend E2E PASS: forgot-password link on /login, both steps render, unknown-email shows generic note (no code), registered email shows 6-digit code in card with copy button, mismatched passwords blocks submission with toast, valid reset redirects to /login, and user can sign in with new password. Aesthetic stays calm/dreamy/sky as required. One real backend bug surfaced — see action_items.

minor.issue: Email casing mismatch: /api/auth/register stores email AS-IS (e.g. 'Foo@Bar.com'), but /api/auth/forgot-password lowercases the lookup ('email = payload.email.lower().strip()'). Result: any user who registered with an uppercase letter in their email cannot get a reset code — the endpoint silently returns code=null (treated as unregistered). Login has the same case-sensitive behavior. Recommend normalizing email to lowercase at registration (and login/session) OR using a case-insensitive index/query in all three endpoints. This is why the first pytest run failed; tests now use lowercase emails as a workaround.

passed_tests: POST /api/auth/forgot-password registered email → {message, code: 6-digit string, expires_in_seconds: 900}
POST /api/auth/forgot-password unregistered email → same shape, code=null (no enumeration leak)
POST /api/auth/reset-password happy path → 200, login with new password works, OLD password returns 401
POST /api/auth/reset-password invalid code → 400 'Invalid or expired code'
POST /api/auth/reset-password reused code → 400 'Invalid or expired code' (single-use enforced; also invalidates other outstanding codes for the email)
POST /api/auth/reset-password new_password<6 chars → 400 'Password must be at least 6 characters'
Regression: register / login / me / logout, questions variety+randomization, answer correct/wrong, leaderboard, my-rank, characters list+purchase+equip, daily-reward status+claim, profile — all PASS
Frontend: /login shows 'Forgot your password?' link (data-testid=forgot-password-link) → navigates to /forgot-password
Frontend: /forgot-password Step 1 renders forgot-email-input, forgot-request-code-btn, forgot-back-to-login
Frontend: Unknown email shows forgot-code-not-found note (no forgot-code-display rendered)
Frontend: Registered email shows forgot-code-display + forgot-code-value with 6-digit code + forgot-code-copy button + expiry text
Frontend: Mismatched passwords shows 'Passwords do not match' toast and does NOT call /api/auth/reset-password (URL remains /forgot-password)
Frontend: Full E2E — register → /forgot-password → request code → enter code + new password → submit → redirected to /login → sign in with new password → /dashboard
action_items: BACKEND BUG (minor): normalize email at registration/login/session to lowercase (or use case-insensitive lookups everywhere). Today, a user who registers with 'Alice@Example.com' cannot reset their password because forgot_password lowercases the lookup. Fix in /app/backend/server.py: lowercase email in register, login, session, forgot-password, reset-password consistently — or apply a unique case-insensitive index on db.users.email.
critical_code_review_comments: Email casing inconsistency (described in backend_issues.minor) — should be addressed; current behavior is a silent no-op for users with mixed-case emails.
ResetPasswordRequest.code is typed as `str` and reset endpoint requires it — pydantic 422 surfaces correctly when code is missing/null; good.
Forgot-password endpoint correctly returns same shape for unknown email and rate-cap hit — no enumeration leakage. Good.
Reset endpoint invalidates all outstanding codes AND all sessions on success — defense in depth, very nice.
Codes hashed with bcrypt at rest — secure. 6-digit numeric is brute-force friendly though; 3-active-code cap mitigates this reasonably.

TTL index commented in startup but not actually created on `expires_at` (because expires_at is stored as ISO string, not BSON Date). Old reset rows will accumulate. Consider storing expires_at as a real datetime to enable MongoDB TTL cleanup. Non-blocking.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all forgot-password testids, both paths, mismatch guard, E2E reset+login all verified)

test_credentials: Tests create ephemeral users via /api/auth/register with lowercase test_fp_*@example.com / DreamySky123!.
seed_data_creation: None added. db.password_resets collection auto-populated by /auth/forgot-password during tests; codes are bcrypt-hashed and marked used after reset.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run regression with: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_kite_trivia.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml. The 7 forgot/reset tests live in the same file. IMPORTANT: forgot-password endpoint lowercases the email lookup while register stores as-is — keep test emails lowercase. The pending email-casing fix in /app/backend/server.py is the only known backend gap. Frontend forgot-password page testids: forgot-password-page, forgot-email-input, forgot-request-code-btn, forgot-back-to-login, forgot-code-display, forgot-code-value, forgot-code-copy, forgot-code-not-found, forgot-code-input, forgot-new-password-input, forgot-confirm-password-input, forgot-reset-btn, forgot-start-over-btn.
rca of the issue: Forgot-password returning code=null for registered users was traced to /app/backend/server.py line 399 (`email = payload.email.lower().strip()`) vs register (line 180 stores raw `user_data.email`). MongoDB find_one is case-sensitive, so mixed-case originals never match the lowercased query. Mitigation: lowercase emails uniformly across register/login/session OR add a `case-insensitive collation` or `email_lower` indexed field used by all auth lookups.
